recentItems.description:

recentItems.title: Economy hits its speed limit, raising RBA rate rise chance | The Business | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
Australia's economy grew 0.4 per cent in the June quarter, slightly beating most economist forecasts and further raising the prospect of an interest rate hike as soon as this month. The economy grew 2.1 per cent over the past year to June 30, seasonally adjusted, according to the latest Australian Bureau of Statistics National Accounts. Treasurer Jim Chalmers says it's proof the Australian economy is as strong or stronger than every other major advanced economy but he did concede it is facing a number of challenges from flat productivity to high inflation and global volatility.

Household consumption grew 0.4 per cent in the quarter and contributed about half of Australia's overall economic growth during the three months to June 30. Discretionary spending was the driver, but the ABS said nearly half of the 1.4 per cent jump in the category was due to a surge in vehicle purchases.

Traders have subsequently pushed up the odds of a September interest rate hike by the Reserve Bank of Australia to about 70 per cent, according to Bloomberg analysis of futures market pricing.

recentItems.title: What is going on in the bond market? | The Business | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
AMP's head of investment strategy and chief economist, Shane Oliver says the spike in global bond yields shows what bond markets think of the Trump administration's management of the US economy.

At time of recording, bond yields are sitting at around a 15-year high, above 5 per cent.

He says bond vigilantes have 'suddenly' come back to the fore, and many of the the reasons that interest rates have gone up in the US come back to Donald Trump.

 "They're acting with their feet saying, 'look, if you're going to keep doing this, keep borrowing all this money, then we're going to get a little bit nervous and we may not lend you as much money' and that puts upwards pressure on bond yields," he says.

In Australia, bond markets were pricing in interest rates moving higher, with the Australian 10-year at a 15-year high today.

Mr Oliver says many of the factors behind rising Australian bond yields are global, and relate to the US.

"The tariffs put upwards pressure on US prices. He then engages in a war with Iran, which has achieved next to nothing except higher oil prices, that adds to inflation... So it's quite possible if we didn't have Donald Trump, America would be looking at lower interest rates and bond yields would not be where they are right now," he said. 
#ABCBusiness

recentItems.title: Pill test trial results lead to it becoming permanent at NSW music festivals | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
Pill testing will be made permanent in New South Wales after a trial at music festivals was linked to a decrease in drug-related hospitalisations.
 
The Minns government will provide a drug checking service at up to 15 festivals per year, beginning in October.
 
The trial, recommended by the drug summit in December 2024, ran for one year from March 2025.
 
NSW Health carried out testing at 12 festivals, with more than 1,800 people visiting the service and almost 1,500 samples analysed.
 
An evaluation by the University of Sydney found the drug checking service was associated with reduced rates of drug-related hospital presentations.
 
There were 2.3 hospital presentations per festival day during the trial, compared to an average of 3.6 over the previous two years.
 
"A trend towards decreasing hospital presentations during the trial year is seen," the report states.
 
"This was seen across festivals of all sizes and music styles."
 
#ABCNewsNSW
